name: Why is my faucet making a strange noise?

mainEntity.name: Why is my faucet making a strange noise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Strange noises from your faucet, such as squealing, whistling, banging, or chattering, often indicate specific internal issues. A squealing sound might suggest a worn-out washer or a damaged cartridge. Whistling can be due to mineral buildup or a partially closed valve restricting water flow. Banging noises (water hammer) usually point to loose pipes or sudden changes in water pressure. Chattering can stem from a loose stem assembly or internal component. Identifying the exact cause typically requires a professional inspection to determine the appropriate repair.
acceptedAnswer.description: Strange faucet noises like squealing, whistling, or banging often indicate worn parts, mineral buildup, or water pressure issues requiring professional diagnosis.
